titulo: The brain: cloud or local, decided with your numbers
lead: The AI model is the easiest part to swap. In the cloud, OpenRouter gives you access to more than a hundred models with one key. On your computer, Ollama runs at no cost per message and sends nothing outside your machine. The choice isn't a matter of taste: it's a table with speed, quality, and cost.
objetivo: compare one cloud model and one local model using the same question, then decide what to use each for based on your numbers.

aprende.t: Why changing the brain doesn't change the rest
Build the speed × quality × cost table
Where the cloud key is stored

hero_alt: A small desktop computer beside a laptop, with cables neatly arranged on a dark desk.

nos.detalhe: The loop doesn't know which model is on the other end. It sends the conversation and the list of tools, then waits for a reply.

A provider is a contract: it receives the conversation and the tools, then returns a reply. In tests, a mock provider responds without internet or cost. To change brains, switch providers in the configuration.
One key gives you access to Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama, and others. It automatically retries when the service fails and tracks the tokens used, so you can control the cost.
The model runs locally. You need a computer that can handle it (memory and, preferably, a graphics card). In the INTELECTO plan, it’s also the automatic backup if OpenRouter fails.

secoes.legenda: Cloud for power, local for privacy. You can use both.

texto: Choose a question you would actually ask the assistant, preferably one related to a task in your meu-jarvis.md.
Use exactly the same text with both models.

exemplo.texto: Organize these into three priorities: finish the sales report, reply to two clients, and prepare for Thursday’s meeting.

texto: Time it from sending until the full response arrives. Run it twice: the first call to the local model is usually slower because it needs to load.

exemplo.texto: Time in seconds, cloud and local.

texto: Read both responses without knowing which is which, if you can ask someone to switch their order. Rate each from 1 to 5: Was it accurate? Did it follow your style? Was it useful?
A short note for each response is enough.

exemplo.texto: Would I use this response without rewriting it? Yes = 4 or 5.

texto: For the cloud model, check the OpenRouter dashboard to see how much the question cost. Locally, each message costs nothing; the cost is keeping the computer on.
Write your decision in one line: which model for what.

exemplo.texto: Daily routine locally; client messages in the cloud.

Decision: I’ll use ____ for ____ and ____ for ____.

abas.html:
• Difficult questions, long text, and multi-step reasoning.
  • A computer without enough memory or a graphics card for a good local model.
  • You’re willing to pay for usage and send the text outside your machine.

• Sensitive data that can’t leave the machine.
  • Many simple messages per day, where usage costs would add up.
  • Working without internet, or as a backup when the cloud goes down.

exercicios.texto: Run the same question through a cloud model (OpenRouter) and a local one (Ollama), if your computer can handle it. Fill in the minha-comparacao.md table.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: When does a local model (Ollama) make sense?
opcoes: When your computer can handle it and your numbers for speed, quality, and cost show it is worth it, or when the data cannot leave your machine.
Never, Telegram does not support it.
Only in the middle of the night.
perguntas.explica: The choice is based on measurement: same question in both, table, decision. Privacy is the other strong reason: with a local model, nothing leaves your machine.

perguntas.p: You switched from OpenRouter to Ollama. What needs to change in the channel and memory?
opcoes: Everything: the channel and memory depend on the model.
Nothing: the provider is a contract, and the rest of the agent does not know which model is responding.
perguntas.explica: The loop calls the provider through the contract. Switching brains is a configuration change; the tests run the same way.

perguntas.p: Why run the question twice on the local model before recording the time?
opcoes: Because the first answer is always wrong.
Because the first call is usually slower while the model loads.
perguntas.explica: A fair comparison measures normal use. The first call includes loading the model into memory.
